summary.headline: Kalyan Jewellers Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 38% to INR10,008 crore and PAT to INR349 crore, helped by a one-off customs duty gain.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue (net of bullion) grew 38% YoY to INR10,008 crore, with EBITDA of INR633 crore (vs INR508 crore) and PAT of INR349 crore (vs INR264 crore). India revenue rose to INR8,503 crore and Middle East to about INR1,320 crore, while Candere turned PAT positive at INR2.1 crore. Management attributed part of profit to a one-time customs duty gain of about INR40-41 crore that was passed to customers via old gold exchange offers, and flagged a 0.2-0.3% PBT margin dilution from exchange. Management said the PBT margin for the full year should hold at or above FY26 levels on a conservative basis.

segments.name: India (Kalyan)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR8,503 crore (+38% YoY) and EBITDA INR500 crore (+15%); PAT INR321 crore (+25%). Management said non-South markets now contribute 50-60% of revenue.

segments.name: Middle East
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR1,320 crore (+29%), EBITDA INR90 crore (vs INR73 crore), profit INR25 crore (vs INR22 crore).

segments.name: Candere (e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR141 crore (vs INR66 crore, roughly double); profit INR2.1 crore vs loss of INR10 crore. Management targets around 50 new Candere stores in FY27 and said Candere stays PAT positive for the year.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 PBT margin expected to be at least in line with FY26 on a conservative basis; exchange dilution of 0.2-0.3% to be offset by cash-for-gold, which is margin accretive.
Customs duty related gain expected at about INR60 crore in Q2 FY27, with some further benefit possible in the running quarter, though management said part may be shared with consumers.
Store expansion target unchanged: 84 Kalyan showrooms and about 50 Candere stores in FY27; H2 is typically heavier than H1. Management cites 70-80 showrooms a year overall.

Non-GML debt to be fully repaid by end-September 2026; second tranche of real estate collaterals to be released thereafter. Management said the company would be debt-free on a non-GML basis in a couple of months.
Recycled gold share to be maintained at 55-60% of revenue going forward.
Real estate sale: agreements signed for two land parcels for about INR102 crore; sale expected to close and proceeds received before end of Q1 FY27 (June quarter).
capex_capacity: Expansion is mainly franchise-led (FOCO model, where the franchisee funds capex and inventory and Kalyan runs the store for a margin share); franchisee ROCE cited at about 14%.
Kalyan ROCE rose to about 20% from the late teens; management expects further improvement from capital-light expansion.

New regional brand Akshaya Thanga Maligai (ATM) for Tamil Nadu: first showroom in Chennai on 21 August 2026, with four more showrooms planned in the following months, including other cities; expansion also to be predominantly FOCO.
Q1 FY27 saw 12 FOCO store openings, per the analyst's question; management confirmed no change to annual targets.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as robust except for about one month of Adhik Maas, when wedding demand slowed in parts of the country. Management said July demand was strong and continuing like Q1, but declined to quantify the trend.
Gold prices corrected about 15-20% over 2-3 months; management said customers buy by budget, so volumes rise when prices fall.
Recycled gold ('Shine with India' campaign) rose to over 46% of revenue in Q1, with June above 55%, as oil-driven forex pressure pushed the company to reduce imported gold.
Cash-for-gold (new product) grew from single-digit share in Q1 to double-digit share as of the call; management said peers are also adopting it.

Exchange transactions are priced at the board rate; cash purchases of old gold are at a discount to spot, which management said is margin accretive. Bullion sales in Q1 were used to fund cash needs of vendors, mainly studded vendors on invoice basis.
Employee cost rose about 54% YoY standalone; management said this is more than the usual annual increment and worth about 0.2-0.3% of revenue, offset by operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any bonus issue planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no bonus share plans as of now.

qa_highlights.question: Ex the one-off gain of INR410 crore, standalone PBT growth was only about 14%, so what drove the margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PBT margin ex-bullion was about 5.1% vs 5.5-5.6% earlier. The gain was partly passed to consumers via exchange offers (INR30-40 crore), exchange dilutes margin by 0.2-0.3%, and platinum/silver one-offs of about 0.2% were absent.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 0.2-0.3% exchange-related dilution persist for the next two to three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no for full year: cash-for-gold should offset exchange dilution, and it expects FY27 PBT margin at least in line with FY26 on a conservative basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gold price fall boosting volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customers come with a budget, so lower gold prices mechanically raise volumes; wedding demand cannot pause more than 2-3 weeks, and discretionary demand may pause about 1-1.5 months.

qa_highlights.question: How much customs duty benefit is expected in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR60 crore in Q2, with some benefit possible in the running quarter but part to be shared with consumers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Candere?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Candere has been PAT positive since 2H FY26, will stay positive in FY27, and will add about 50 stores with focus on inventory throughput in existing stores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee cost increase one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not one-time; it is above the usual annual increment, occurs once every few years, and operating leverage should absorb it.

risks_watch: Margin: exchange-led volumes dilute PBT margin by 0.2-0.3%; the full-year margin target depends on cash-for-gold scaling up.
One-off customs duty gains (about INR41 crore in Q1, about INR60 crore expected in Q2) may not recur and partly go to consumers.
Gold price volatility (15-20% correction) may pause discretionary demand and push customers to change grammage/price points.
Employee cost up about 54% YoY standalone; watch whether operating leverage offsets it.
Execution of non-GML debt repayment by September 2026 and the real estate sale proceeds.
Management declined to comment on governance questions raised in the press about related-party transactions; an open overhang for investors.
ATM's ramp-up and whether the regional format can scale beyond the first five stores.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and demand, citing strong July trading and a 38% revenue rise. Somewhat evasive on quantifying the July trend, the Adhik Maas impact and governance questions, and reliant on cash-for-gold to offset margin dilution, which is not yet proven.
key_quotes: Q1 performance has been very satisfactory given the overall context.
The quarter has started off very well despite the volatility in gold prices.
Candere has been PAT positive for the first quarter and should continue for this financial year.
For the full year, I don't think there will be an impact. Even on a conservative basis, I think we'll be able to maintain the PBT margins of the previous year.
